concept: One request, one board. A single login form travels from a browser card to a server card across an open path, past a slate router box that is the watcher. The board never changes layout: each step adds one thing (a certificate, two keys, a scrambled packet), and the watcher's copy tray shows what it has learned at every step: readable text, two useless values, no key, only noise. The padlock that opens on the promise closes on the payoff.

story.metaphor: An open road with a watcher at the crossroads: what it can read tells you how private the message is.
story.setting: A single clean diagram board on the light corporate field; no people, no sets.
story.arc: Readable and exposed, then identity checked, key agreed, data scrambled, a failed check tested, the padlock read honestly, and the opening frame returns with the watcher holding only noise.

devices.what: The form packet: a card of readable fields that shape-morphs into scrambled blocks when it passes the key, and back again at the far end. Same object every time it crosses.
The tray under the router box that holds the watcher's copy: readable fields in s1, two copied values and an empty key slot in s3, the same noise in s4 and the payoff.

The certificate card: site name, expiry and issuer rows with an authority seal; ticks stamp in teal one row at a time, it shrinks to a ticked badge, re-lights on recall, and its name row turns red in the check.

Swap slots: one empty key slot at each end and one by the watcher. Matching blue keys drop into the end slots only; the watcher's slot stays empty. The key then sits on the path ends as the lens the packet passes through.
One generic padlock: appears open above the path on the promise, carries the habit labels, closes on the payoff.
Join device: the camera pans along the held board and pushes into the part the voice names, then pulls back to the wide board. Hard cuts only at the check, the habit station and the payoff return.

parts.what: The whole HTTPS path board at fixed coordinates: browser card (window chrome, a login form with User and Password fields filled with readable sample text and a Submit button), server card (a simple server glyph and a name strip 'accounts.example'), a thin path line between them, a slate router box mid-path with a small watcher mark (a box with an eye-like aperture, not a person), a copy tray under the router with named contents, and the watcher's own key slot. Flat rounded cards, soft shadow, angular corners. Must read on the light field and on the navy dark band (cards stay surface, lines lighten). Can draw the server card alone at small scale (opts.only: 'server') for the address bar inset, and can relabel the browser address strip.

The form packet: a small card with two readable rows (User, Password) in ink; it morphs into a row of six angular scrambled blocks filled with random glyph texture, and back. Also a reply variant with two readable lines.

A certificate card: header 'Certificate', rows 'Site name: accounts.example', 'Valid until' with an in-range bar (no date digits), 'Issued by: Example Authority', an authority seal bottom right. Teal tick per row; can shrink to a 120 px ticked badge; name row can turn red with a cross and show a different name 'other-site.example'.
Three swap slots (80x80 rounded squares with dashed outline): browser end, server end, watcher. A blue key glyph drops into a slot; the end keys can glow as a lens the packet passes through.
One generic padlock (no real browser's icon): body and shackle, open and closed states, an enlarged version and a small in-bar version.

A large generic browser address bar: rounded pill, padlock slot at left, site name 'accounts.example' that can highlight letter by letter, and an optional empty warning slot under it reading 'Certificate warning: none'.

kit.notes: Keys are always blue (accent) and mean the shared secret; ticks are teal (pos); the red cross (neg) appears only in b14. Value tokens (b07) and option flags (b14) are drawn inline with the tech seed's flag labels.
